column1: # derivation: §7.4: concat_ws(sep, a, ...) is NULL when sep is NULL;
# a NULL argument is skipped together with its separator; '' is a value
# (§7.12) and is kept with its separator. Row id 8 is filtered out (id <> 8,
# §1.2): with s and t both NULL every argument is skipped and §7.4 does not
# say what remains. ws = concat_ws('|', s, t): 1 "abc|x"; 2 t NULL, "h"
# U+00E9 "llo"; 3 s then "|" then '': s followed by "|"; 4 "a" U+1F600
# "b|-"; 5 '' with t NULL skipped: ''; 6 s NULL skipped: "y"; 7 s "|"
# U+00C4 U+00D6; 9 U+1F600 "|" U+FF21. ws_sep = concat_ws(t, s, 'Q'): t is
# the separator, so rows 2 and 5 (t NULL) are NULL; 1 "abcxQ"; 3 sep '':
# s then "Q"; 4 "a" U+1F600 "b-Q"; 6 s NULL skipped with its separator:
# Types: a string (§7.4); §8 has no row for CONCAT_WS, so nullable by §8's
# default (ws_sep does hold NULLs); id as scanned.
